title: Interdisciplinary Research Funding Gaps
bottleneck: The biggest problems span disciplines, but funding, hiring, and journals are organized by discipline, penalizing researchers who work across boundaries. Interdisciplinary proposals face reviewers from no single field who feel qualified to judge them, and tenure committees discount cross-field work. Review panels assembled across fields often lack the expertise to evaluate novel combinations, defaulting to safe disciplinary work.
why_it_blocks: Disciplinary silos slow progress exactly where the hardest problems live. The most important questions sit precisely at the boundaries panels are worst at judging. Structural reform of review, not just exhortation, is required.
current_state: Interdisciplinary programs exist but are small; the core incentive structure of academia remains disciplinary. Dedicated interdisciplinary institutes with their own tenure lines are the structural fix, rarely implemented.

sources.title: Evidence and the Design and Reform of Scientific Institutions (Nintil)
